module_title: Gandhian Era (1919-1939) - Swaraj Party, Simon Commission, and Civil Disobedience
introduction: At this level, we explore the political vacuum created after the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement, the historic demand for 'Purna Swaraj', the Dandi March, and the rising influence of revolutionary socialists like Bhagat Singh.

core_concepts.title: Swaraj Party (1923)
core_concepts.description: Formed by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru after the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement. Their goal was to contest council elections and obstruct government functioning from within (they were called Pro-changers).

core_concepts.title: Simon Commission (1927-1928)
core_concepts.description: A statutory commission led by Sir John Simon arrived in India to review the 1919 Act. Since all its 7 members were British (an 'All-White Commission'), it was boycotted nationwide with the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.

core_concepts.title: Lahore Session and Purna Swaraj (1929)
core_concepts.description: Under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the INC declared 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) as its ultimate goal and decided to celebrate January 26, 1930, as the first Independence Day.

core_concepts.title: Civil Disobedience Movement & Dandi March (1930)
core_concepts.description: Gandhi started the historic Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930, with 78 followers. He broke the salt law at Dandi on April 6, 1930, officially launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

core_concepts.title: Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)
core_concepts.description: An agreement signed on March 5, 1931, between Viceroy Lord Irwin and Gandhi (Delhi Pact). The Civil Disobedience Movement was suspended, and the Congress agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.

important_entities.name: C.R. Das (Chittaranjan Das)
important_entities.significance: The founding President of the Swaraj Party.

important_entities.name: Lala Lajpat Rai
important_entities.significance: Succumbed to injuries sustained during a brutal police lathi-charge while protesting against the Simon Commission in Lahore.

important_entities.name: Bhagat Singh
important_entities.significance: Founded the HSRA (Hindustan Socialist Republican Association) and popularized the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Nehru Report was prepared by 'Motilal Nehru', not Jawaharlal Nehru. It was the first major attempt by Indians to draft a constitutional framework.
The march lasted exactly 24 days (March 12 to April 6). Students often confuse the distance (240 miles) with the number of days.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Simon needs Lahore to do Civil Ir-winning
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Simon Commission (1927) -> Nehru Report (1928) -> Lahore Session (1929) -> Civil Disobedience/Dandi (1930) -> Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

exam_strategy_tips: Chronology-based questions are extremely common for the 1927-1931 period. Master the exact sequence of events.
A frequent factual question: How many followers accompanied Gandhi on the Dandi March? (Answer: 78).
